President François Hollande (pictured in 2013) was at the Stade de France during the attacks.

Three groups, comprising three men each, executed the attacks.[29][57] They wore explosive vests and belts with identical detonators.[104] Seven perpetrators died at the scenes of their attacks.[6][105] The other two were killed five days later during the Saint-Denis police raid.[106] The tenth participant, Salah Abdeslam, drove the Stade de France bombers to the stadium.
He was supposed to execute a suicide bombing in the 18th arrondissement after dropping off the group, but he never did and disposed of his explosive vest.
A woman cries as she stands at the Le Carillon bar on 14 November 2015.

On 15 November, the French Air Force launched the biggest airstrike of Opération Chammal, its bombing campaign against ISIL, sending 10 aircraft to drop 20 bombs on Raqqa, the city where ISIL is based.[137] On 16 November, the French Air Force carried out more airstrikes on ISIL targets in Raqqa, including a command centre and a training camp.[213] On 18 November 2015, French aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle left its home port of Toulon heading towards the eastern Mediterranean to support bombing operations carried out by the international coalition.[214] This decision was taken before the November attacks but was accelerated by the events.

French Interior Minister Bernard Cazeneuve said that he would meet with EU ministers to discuss how to deal with terrorism across the European Union.[230] Meeting reports indicated that Schengen area border controls have been tightened for EU citizens entering or leaving, with passport checks[231] and systematic screening against biometric databases.
The state of emergency was extended until the end of July 2016.[263] Further extensions followed after the attack in Nice on 14 July 2016.

On 5 October 2022, the French film November was released, directed by Cédric Jimenez and starring Jean Dujardin, that depicts the investigations and the interventions of the police (in particular of the anti-terrorist sub-directorate) during the five days which followed the attacks.
Alice Winocour's 2022 feature film Revoir Paris[307] (Paris Memories) looked at the effects of the aftermath of a group of people trapped in an attached bistro and starred Virginie Efira.
A 4-part miniseries named Les Espions de la Terreur was released by M6 in 2024.
It shows the aftermath of the November attacks through the eyes of the French Secret Service.
